title: The Core Secret of Java Collections

scenes.line1: Why do equals and hashCode matter?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why equals and hashCode are such a big deal in Java? Let’s crack the contract that makes collections work.

scenes.label: HashMap
scenes.sub: Uses hashCode to find buckets, equals to check matches.
scenes.say: HashMap, and also HashSet, rely on hashCode to find the right bucket, and equals to check if two objects are really the same.

rows.b: If A equals B, hash codes must match
If hash codes match, equals still checks
If A not equal B, hash codes can differ

scenes.say: Here’s the contract: If two objects are equal, their hash codes must match. If hash codes match, equals still checks for true equality. If objects aren’t equal, hash codes can be different.
If you override equals but forget hashCode, collections like HashSet or HashMap won’t work as expected. Your object might disappear or duplicate.

scenes.question: Can you skip hashCode if equals is custom?
scenes.right: No! Both must be consistent for collections to work.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic trap: Can you skip hashCode if you override equals? No way. Both must match, or your collections break.
